transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I keep seeing that explosion in my head like it’s happening all over again, and I can’t shut it off. It just plays over and over, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Can you tell me if this explosion you keep reliving was something you experienced directly, or witnessed, and did it involve actual or threatened death or serious injury?

Yes, I was right there in the basement when the gas ignited, and we both got trapped in the fire. I barely made it out with some burns, but my young apprentice was severely injured and ended up dying in the hospital. It was very real, and it took his life while nearly taking mine.
Do you have nightmares or flashbacks about the event, and do you feel emotionally numb or detached from others since it happened?

Yes, I have terrible flashbacks during the day where I feel like I'm right back in that exploding basement, and at night I wake up gasping from recurring nightmares about the fire. I also feel completely numb and detached, like I'm just watching someone else's life, which has made me pull away from my family and church because I can't feel happiness or love anymore.
Do you avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the explosion, and do you feel constantly on edge, jumpy, or easily startled?

Yeah, I'll drive the long way around just to avoid older buildings or that side of town, and I walk away if anyone at church brings up the accident. I'm also incredibly jumpy; if someone drops a tool at work or slams a car door, I jump out of my skin and it takes me a long time to stop shaking.
